page: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.8xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz. The configuration provides 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with 2 threads per core, backed by 64.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz. This yields a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The processor includes a 105 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512). It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it features a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-threaded performance, with the single-core Geekbench score and single-threaded gzip compression placing in the top 25% tier. Cryptographic capabilities are also strong, as evidenced by the PassMark CPU encryption test. Multi-core and memory-bound operations generally fall within the average range, with a PassMark CPU score of 48,904.2 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 15,951.0. The instance demonstrates strong static web serving throughput at 51.12 GB/sec, alongside average performance in software compilation and database operations. Small-model LLM text generation is strong at 286.26 tokens per second, though medium-model inference speeds remain average.

As part of the c7i-flex family, this instance offers a cost-efficient alternative for compute-heavy workloads that do not require the full continuous performance of standard c7i instances. The primary tradeoff is the lack of local NVMe storage, requiring reliance on network-attached storage, and the baseline network limit of 6 Gbps. The instance is suited for workloads such as static web serving, single-threaded data compression, lightweight machine learning inference, and general-purpose compute tasks that benefit from modern Intel Xeon instruction sets like AMX and AVX-512.
